content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have a [product_name] 24 ([article_no]) that's malfunctioning. Can I replace it with a [product_name] 24 ([article_no])? I appreciate any advice. Best regards!

Hello [user_name]. Based on my experience, you can use [article_no] as a replacement, but note that [article_no] uses transistor outputs, while [article_no] has relay outputs. In this case, I recommend placing a relay after the transistor output—something like a 2-contact relay (2NC - 2NO, 10A)—for protection. Generally, transistor outputs respond faster than relays when you need low response times. Best regards.
Thank you [user_name]! Is it possible to use [product_name] 24C ([article_no]) as a substitute for [product_name] 24 ([article_no])?

Yes, you can. Both modules have 24VDC transistor outputs and analog inputs. Note that the newer module ([article_no]) offers 4 analog inputs and has a real-time clock, while the older one has 2 analog inputs.
[user_name], yes, replacement is possible. Best regards.
Thank you all! So I can swap the modules and transfer the uploaded program from [article_no] to [article_no]? Will my system function as usual?
Yes, your system should work normally. Just make sure to update the hardware configuration in the file from [article_no] to [article_no].
